summary: Round 2 re-review of b36e7df. Round-1: F-1 fixed (sdd 4.1 session states, silent probe 401, session-ended only when signed-in, tests); F-2 fixed (4.2 safeReturnTo allow-list, tests); F-3 fixed (5 explicit White_Space set, NBSP tests, 12.1 item 4); F-4 fixed (6 ProblemWriter for all error sources, contract adds 405/415/REQUEST_REJECTED codes, per-source test); F-5 fixed (11, ADR-0013 test-only offset clock); F-6 fixed (ADR-0007..0017); F-7 fixed (9, NFR-001 row); F-8, F-9 fixed (12.1 items 1-3); F-10 carried as info. Contract and SDD agree on codes, 401 precedence, 415 rule and session states. No blocker or major. Two minors: 12.1 omits returnTo landing and the no-message reload after expiry; approver confirms at freeze, no requester decision needed before freeze.

findings.message: The returnTo behaviour (4.2) sends a user to /todos/<uuid>, /todos/<uuid>/edit or /todos/new after login. REQ-AUTH-002 AC-1 says the user is signed in and sees their own to-do list, and REQ-AUTH-004 AC-2 only requires sending the user to the login page; no requirement or answer asks for a return to the deep link. This is a product-visible choice not listed in 12.1.
findings.suggestion: Add returnTo to 12.1 (after login the user returns to the to-do route they opened, otherwise /todos) so the approver confirms it at freeze, or reduce safeReturnTo to /todos with its list query only.

findings.message: Reload after expiry (4.1) lands the user on the bare login page with no session-ended message, because the SPA no longer holds a user. The SDD argues the login page itself is the request to log in again for REQ-AUTH-004 AC-4; defensible, but it is an interpretation of AC-4 (the message appears only when a signed-in tab makes a request) and is not listed in 12.1.
findings.suggestion: List it in 12.1 for the approver, or show the message after reload by keeping a non-secret was-signed-in flag (for example sessionStorage) cleared on logout; keep the component test for whichever is chosen.

findings.message: Search and identifier matching use a simple Locale.ROOT lower-case mapping, not full case folding (for example ss vs sharp s); the risk table records it as Accepted but no requester or approver accepted it, and 12.1 does not list it. Narrow effect on REQ-LIST-002 AC-1 (identifiers are ASCII, so uniqueness is unaffected).
findings.suggestion: Optionally add a one-line item to 12.1 so the acceptance is the approvers,nottheauthors.

findings.message: The rationale for not using Java String.strip says Java omits U+00A0, U+2007, U+202F and adds U+001C-U+001F; Character.isWhitespace also omits U+0085 (NEL), which is in the chosen set. The design is unaffected because both sides use an explicit list and a shared test table that includes U+0085.
findings.suggestion: Add U+0085 to the list of code points Java omits.

findings.message: Residual ADR bundling after the split: ADR-0016 combines pool size, WAL, foreign_keys and busy_timeout (only pool size and WAL have alternatives); ADR-0005 combines the hashing algorithm with the login timing defence (dummy hash) and the over-128 refusal at login; ADR-0002 combines Java version, build tool, servlet stack and module layout. These are cohesive enough and alternatives are given; hygiene only.
findings.suggestion: No action needed for freeze; split the login timing defence out of ADR-0005 if ADRs are revisited.

findings.message: The order of checks is stated only for protected unsafe requests. On an unprotected path a POST/PUT/DELETE with a wrong method or unknown route (for example POST /api/v1/nope or PUT /api/v1/auth/login) without X-Todo-Client gets 403 from ClientHeaderFilter before 404/405. Consistent with the contract rule that every POST, PUT and DELETE needs the header, but not written down.
findings.suggestion: Optionally add one sentence: on unprotected paths the header check (403) precedes route and method (404/405); the NFR-004 unknown-route test uses GET.

findings.message: Carried from round-1 F-10: the requirements.md sha256 in the sdd.md frontmatter is not verified by this review (no hashing tool in the critic grant); requirements.md is not in the 6695a40..b36e7df diff, so it is unchanged since round 1. Squad PR #2 (java-engineer, react-engineer) still awaits the requester merge; delivery risk only, recorded in section 13.
findings.suggestion: Orchestrator checks the upstream hash at freeze; requester merges PR #2 before the build phase.
